To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the coupling of projector-based embedding and quantum mechanics/molecular mechanisms is a robust and efficient method to calculate energies and geometries of enzyme reactions; (ii) the method is applicable to reactions involving proton transfers and to reactions involving transition metal centers; and (iii) the method is robust and accurate, even when using a low-cost density-functional approximation for the embedding.

the coupling of projector-based embedding with quantum mechanics and molecular mechanics modeling allows for the calculation of high-accuracy energies for the proton-abstraction reaction of acetyl-coenzymeA catalyzed by citrate synthases, and that the method can be applied to other enzymes.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the combination of projector-embedding theory and quantum mechanics/molecular mechanical modeling can be applied to large-scale chemical systems and is a viable alternative to the traditional QM/MM method.

projector-embedding calculations are a viable alternative for multiscale calculations in enzyme-catalyved reactions, and they are likely to be more efficient than the traditional approach of embedding correlated wavefunction methods in a molecular mechanics potential energy surface.

the combination of embedding and quantum mechanics/molecular mechanisms is a powerful approach to study complex systems, such as enzymes, where quantum mechanics is required in only a few active-site residues.
